#!/bin/bash

class_name Wear
extends RefCounted
## Tool wear on the CLIENT's Bag item (variant E, W2, plan C10): the server only computes what a blow wore off
## (Impact.wear_of, in the hit report) and builds the swung tool with the sharpness the snapshot carries
## (InputSystem.DULL_SHIFT). The item keeps `worn` (int, Impact.WEAR_UNIT m³ of edge lost); sharpness = Impact.sharp_of.
## Sharpening (the whetstone, sandstone) takes SHARPEN_SHARE of the reserve off `worn` per pass.

const SHARPEN_SHARE := 0.1       # of the reserve, per pass
const SHARPEN_TICKS := 30        # physics ticks between two passes


## The item as a Tools.make tool ({} for matter pieces, empty cells).
static func tool_of(it: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
	if it.is_empty() or it.get("matter", false) or not it.has("slot"):
		return {}
	return Tools.make(int(it.slot), int(it.get("mat", Tools.DEFAULT_MAT)))


## Units of wear on the item (0 = new).
static func worn(it: Dictionary) -> int:
	return int(it.get("worn", 0))


## Edge sharpness 0..1 of an item (1 for what does not wear).
static func sharp(it: Dictionary) -> float:
	var t := tool_of(it)
	return Impact.sharp_of(t, worn(it)) if not t.is_empty() else 1.0


## Does this item's edge wear at all (an axe, a pick, a shovel, not hands / the hammer / food)?
static func wears(it: Dictionary) -> bool:
	var t := tool_of(it)
	return not t.is_empty() and Impact.reserve(t) > 0.0


## Per mille of the sharpness (1000 new .. 0 dull).
static func sharp_pm(it: Dictionary) -> int:
	return roundi(sharp(it) * 1000.0)


## InputSender.tool_dull follows the active hand's item (ItemSettings.sync).
static func sync() -> void:
	InputSender.tool_dull = 1000 - sharp_pm(Hands.hand_a) if not Hands.hand_a.is_empty() else 0


## A blow wore `units` off the tool (slot, mat) in my hands (the report names the tool): the active hand's item when it
## is that tool, else the other hand's.
static func apply(slot: int, mat: int, units: int) -> void:
	if units <= 0:
		return
	for it: Dictionary in [Hands.hand_a, Hands.hand_o]:
		if not it.is_empty() and not it.get("matter", false) and int(it.get("slot", -1)) == slot and wears(it) \
				and int(it.get("mat", Tools.DEFAULT_MAT)) == mat:
			it.worn = worn(it) + units
			Bag.version += 1
			sync()
			return


## One pass on the whetstone: the item in the active hand. Returns the line for the player ("" = nothing to say).
static func sharpen(it: Dictionary) -> String:
	if not wears(it):
		return "Это не точится"
	if worn(it) <= 0:
		return "Лезвие и так острое"
	var r := Impact.reserve(tool_of(it))
	it.worn = maxi(worn(it) - roundi(SHARPEN_SHARE * r / Impact.WEAR_UNIT), 0)
	Bag.version += 1
	sync()
	return "Точу: острота %d %%" % roundi(sharp(it) * 100.0)


## The text of the edge for the HUD: «острота 82 %».
static func line(it: Dictionary) -> String:
	return "острота %d %%" % roundi(sharp(it) * 100.0)
EOF

{"summary": "W2.liquid is done and verified headless only. I ran no browser and took no screenshots (the browser is not allowed in this part), so the bucket model and its hand pose have never been drawn and need a look in the range part.

What exists: a wooden bucket (Tools.BUCKET = 13, "Ведро"), pools with integer litres (−1 = infinite, for the lake), and LiquidSystem with scoop and pour.

- **Bucket:** It is always a one-hand tool and holds 10 L. It sits in the grid of the Bag start set (cell 12); the player moves it onto the belt.
- **Scoop and pour:** LMB aimed at a pool or the valley lake scoops it full. LMB with water in the bucket pours it all out, into a pool if aimed at one (capped by its room), else onto the ground (counted as `spilled`). A partly full bucket can still top up from an infinite pool.
- **Lift check:** All or nothing. A thin body's one hand refuses a full bucket (11 kg > 10 kg limit). A fit body's one hand takes it (28 kg limit). Thin with two hands (25 kg limit) also takes it.
- **Events:** `_pool(id, litres)` and `_bucket(peer, litres)` go to every peer. The bucket litres are mirrored into the owner's Bag item as `litres`. A joiner's client sends `_hello` and the server replies with `_sync`. Litres that arrive before a pool is built are kept and applied when it is.
- **Balance:** A leaving peer's water is added to `spilled`. `balance()` stays constant. It is Σ finite pools + Σ buckets + spilled − `from_infinite`, where `from_infinite` counts litres currently out of infinite pools.

**Day-1 contract (also at the top of notes.md):**
- `LiquidSystem.local()`.
- `use(peer, actor, aim, tool) -> String` ("" = done, else the refusal text).
- `pour(peer, point, litres) -> int`.
- `spill_bucket(peer, point) -> int` is for the drop part: a dropped bucket calls `LiquidSystem.local().spill_bucket(peer, point)`.
- `add_pool(id, floor_pos, size_xz, depth, litres, basin := true) -> Pool` is for the range part (all peers, same arguments). `pool(id)`, `remove_pool(id)`, `total_litres()`, `snapshot()` and `restore()` also exist.
- `LiquidSystem.prompt(actor, tool)` returns a HUD hint line but is not wired into the HUD (step1_hud.gd is W2.wear's file).
- **Landing hook:** In `LootSystem._dropped`, when a stone or timber is created with |v| > 0.5 (a throw), the static `LootSystem._mark_thrown(body)` calls `Landing.mark_thrown(body)`. It loads `res://world/items/landing.gd` by path only if the file exists, so it compiles before landing.gd is written. The stone body is `StoneSystem.Stone.body`, which exists on the server only; on clients it is null and skipped. For wood it passes the Timber node.

E = ½ m v_n², using the velocity of the last frame in the air against the contact normal.\n  - **The thing hit** (a RockNode, or a heavy stone lying on the ground): E passes the hardness gate of the thrown body's material; a fragile target takes the raw E. THIS TASK = variant E, wave 2 (Maxim chose E: 'одна формула для всех материалов E = P·V + R·A + ворота твёрдости + свой невидимый холст у каждого класса', and a material test range near the spawn: 'все материалы листами разной толщины и столбами разного радиуса, побить и проверить физику'). Wave 1 is DONE and published (build/web-final8): 58 material cards (world/items/matter_cards.gd, Matter API), one blow law + hardness gate (world/tools/impact.gd), one hint (world/hud/matter_hint.gd), the range (systems/range_system.gd, world/range/*: rows I wood + II stone + soil bed real, the rest 'скоро' pads). Decisions already told to Maxim (use them): glass / ceramic / ice shards that are big enough go to the pick's flag pile like stones (task 59 StoneSystem flag), small ones become chips/fx (<= 200 loose shards on the range, oldest become fx); the bucket is WOODEN, the lake is infinite; wear: a steel axe needs sharpening after ~30 felled pines, a copper pick after ~66 granite blows; NO 'T' key​ (T / Shift+T = time skip), NO 'K' (debug_kill), NO 'M' (music): sharpening = E (use) on the whetstone stand / a sandstone face in reach if E has no other meaning there, else the free key L; every new key goes into the F1 overlay world/hud/controls_overlay.gd. Player-facing TEXT in Russian, KEY NAMES in English. Maxim's standing feedback: physical, readable cause -> effect; exact volume conservation (what is removed = what lies on the ground); simple low-poly look but pretty; must not lag (browser on a laptop, WebGL2).

NEW in W2 beyond the plan (from the W1 playtest of the range): stone SLABS only dent («скола нет: края рядом нет»), even a 10 mm granite slab hit by a 150 J pick stays whole. By law E the crack runs toward a free face within s_max = sqrt(share·E/(8R)) and the BACK face of a thin plate is a free face. So a thin brittle plate (any brittle kind: granite, sandstone, limestone and the new W2 kinds) must break THROUGH when the crack share pays R·A of a crack across it (A = crack length × thickness): 2 or more pieces by planes through the impact point (PlaneSplit, the same machinery as the fragile shatter), exact volume conservation; thick slabs and big columns keep today's chip/dent behaviour. This belongs to the brittle part.

HUB LIMITS (02.11, the hub ran out of RAM and rebooted, partly because of our tests): the whole T3 service — every agent, godot and Chrome, shared with Maxim's other projects — has 8 CPUs / 49 GiB. Going over lets the OOM killer take the T3 server and every agent dies. So: at most 2 godot processes of yours at a time (the batteries self-cap with JOBS=5 and wait for RAM; only integrate/polish run full batteries); run 'python3 export/hub_guard.py' before a heavy step (it prints free RAM and our cgroup use); the browser ONLY via export/cdp.py (a project-wide lock: one Chrome at a time, it waits for RAM) and only in the range / integrate / polish parts; never a browser and a battery at the same time; kill your servers by PID when done (never pkill -f).
